Incident Response.overview: Design and implement incident response strategies to detect, respond to, and recover from security events in AWS (12% of exam)

key_services.name: AWS CloudTrail
key_services.purpose: Records AWS API calls for account activity and compliance auditing
key_features: Logs all management and data events across AWS services
Delivers logs to S3 with optional encryption via KMS
Log file integrity validation using cryptographic hash
CloudTrail Insights detects unusual API activity automatically
Organization trails log events for all accounts in AWS Organizations
exam_tips: Enable multi-region trails for comprehensive coverage
Use log file validation for forensic investigations
CloudTrail doesn't log data plane events by default (S3 object reads, Lambda executions)
Organization trails simplify compliance for multi-account setups

key_services.name: Amazon GuardDuty
key_services.purpose: Continuous threat detection service using ML to identify malicious activity
key_features: Analyzes VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail events, and DNS logs
Detects cryptocurrency mining, compromised credentials, reconnaissance
Machine learning identifies anomalies and known threats
Integrates with Security Hub and EventBridge for automation
No agents or sensors required
exam_tips: Enable in all regions for comprehensive threat detection
Use EventBridge to automate response to findings
Suppression rules filter false positives
Findings include severity, affected resources, and recommended actions

key_services.name: AWS Security Hub
key_services.purpose: Centralized security and compliance service aggregating findings
key_features: Aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Config, Macie, Inspector, IAM Access Analyzer
Runs automated compliance checks (CIS, PCI-DSS, AWS Foundational Security Best Practices)
Normalizes findings using AWS Security Finding Format (ASFF)
Custom insights and dashboards for security posture
Integrates with 50+ partner security tools
exam_tips: Requires AWS Config to be enabled for compliance checks
Use master-member model for multi-account aggregation
Custom actions trigger automated remediation workflows
Findings are automatically correlated across services

key_services.name: Amazon Detective
key_services.purpose: Analyzes and visualizes security data for rapid investigation
key_features: Automatically processes logs from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty
Creates behavior graphs showing relationships between entities
Stores up to 1 year of historical data
ML-powered anomaly detection in user and resource behavior
Visualizes security event timelines and connections
exam_tips: Requires GuardDuty to be enabled
Use for root cause analysis after GuardDuty finding
Behavior graphs reveal patterns not visible in logs alone
Automatically identifies unusual API calls and network traffic

best_practices: Enable CloudTrail in all regions with log file validation
Configure CloudWatch Events for real-time security alerts
Implement automated response using Lambda and Step Functions
Create incident response playbooks using Systems Manager Automation
Enable GuardDuty across all accounts and regions
Centralize findings in Security Hub for unified visibility
Use AWS Organizations for delegated security service administration
Implement least privilege access for incident responders
Regularly test incident response procedures with game days
Store forensic evidence in S3 with Object Lock for immutability

common_scenarios.compromised_credentials: GuardDuty detects unusual API calls → EventBridge triggers Lambda → Lambda rotates credentials and revokes sessions → SNS notifies security team
common_scenarios.malicious_instance: GuardDuty flags communication with known bad IP → Lambda modifies security group to isolate instance → Systems Manager captures memory dump → SNS alerts team
common_scenarios.data_exfiltration: GuardDuty detects unusual data transfer → Lambda blocks S3 bucket public access → Detective used to investigate full attack path

Logging and Monitoring.overview: Implement comprehensive logging and monitoring solutions to maintain visibility into AWS resource activity and security posture (20% of exam)

key_services.name: Amazon CloudWatch
key_services.purpose: Monitoring and observability service for AWS resources
key_features: CloudWatch Logs for centralized log management
Metric filters extract metrics from logs
CloudWatch Alarms for threshold-based notifications
CloudWatch Insights for log query and analysis
EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) for event-driven workflows
exam_tips: Use metric filters on CloudTrail logs for security events
Logs Insights uses SQL-like query language
Export logs to S3 for long-term retention
Composite alarms combine multiple alarm states

key_services.name: VPC Flow Logs
key_services.purpose: Captures IP traffic information for network interfaces
key_features: Records accepted, rejected, or all traffic
Publishes to CloudWatch Logs or S3
Custom log format with specific fields
Can be enabled at VPC, subnet, or ENI level
exam_tips: Doesn't capture all traffic (DHCP, AWS metadata, Windows license)
Use Athena to query Flow Logs in S3
Analyze rejected traffic to identify security issues
Enable at VPC level for comprehensive coverage

key_services.name: AWS Config
key_services.purpose: Tracks resource configurations and evaluates compliance
key_features: Records configuration changes and history
Config rules check compliance continuously
Conformance packs group rules for standards
Remediation actions use Systems Manager Automation
Relationship tracking between resources
exam_tips: Required for Security Hub compliance checks
Aggregators collect data from multiple accounts/regions
Use managed rules for common compliance checks
Can trigger automatic remediation on drift

best_practices: Enable CloudTrail in all regions with log file validation
Configure VPC Flow Logs for all VPCs
Use CloudWatch Logs encryption with KMS
Implement log retention policies balancing cost and compliance
Enable AWS Config in all accounts and regions
Use Config aggregators for multi-account visibility
Set up CloudWatch metric filters for critical security events
Use Athena for cost-effective log analysis at scale
Enable GuardDuty and Detective for enhanced threat detection
Centralize logs using S3 bucket policies or AWS Organizations

Infrastructure Security.overview: Design and implement secure network architectures and infrastructure protection (26% of exam - largest domain)

key_services.name: Amazon VPC
key_services.purpose: Isolated virtual network for launching AWS resources
key_features: Security groups (stateful firewall at instance level)
Network ACLs (stateless firewall at subnet level)
VPC endpoints for private AWS service access
VPC peering and Transit Gateway for connectivity
Private and public subnets for network segmentation
exam_tips: Security groups are stateful; NACLs are stateless
Default NACL allows all; custom NACLs deny all by default
Security groups support only allow rules; NACLs support allow/deny
Use private subnets with VPC endpoints for zero internet exposure

key_services.name: AWS WAF
key_services.purpose: Web application firewall protecting against common exploits
key_features: Web ACLs with rules and rule groups
AWS Managed Rules auto-updated for threats
Rate-based rules for DDoS mitigation
Custom rules using match conditions
Integrates with CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync
exam_tips: Operates at Layer 7 (application layer)
Use Count mode to test rules before blocking
Managed rule groups cover OWASP Top 10
Can log to S3, CloudWatch Logs, or Kinesis Firehose

key_services.name: AWS Shield
key_features: Shield Standard: automatic network/transport layer protection (free)
Shield Advanced: enhanced DDoS protection with 24/7 DRT support
Cost protection prevents DDoS-related scaling charges
Real-time attack visibility and notifications
Integration with WAF for application layer protection
exam_tips: Shield Standard is automatic and free for all customers
Shield Advanced costs $3,000/month and includes WAF at no charge
DRT (DDoS Response Team) assists during attacks
Cost protection only with Shield Advanced

key_services.name: AWS Network Firewall
key_services.purpose: Managed stateful network firewall for VPCs
key_features: Stateful inspection using Suricata-compatible rules
IPS/IDS capabilities for threat detection
Domain filtering and URL categorization
TLS inspection for encrypted traffic
Centralized management with Firewall Manager
exam_tips: Operates at VPC level, unlike security groups (instance level)
Use for east-west traffic inspection between VPCs
Automatically scales with traffic
Deploy in inspection VPC with Transit Gateway

best_practices: Implement defense in depth with multiple security layers
Use private subnets for sensitive workloads
Enable VPC Flow Logs for network traffic visibility
Use VPC endpoints to avoid internet traffic for AWS services
Enable WAF on all internet-facing applications
Use Shield Advanced for business-critical applications
Implement Network Firewall for advanced threat protection
Use PrivateLink for secure service-to-service communication
Regularly review security group rules for least privilege
Use Transit Gateway for centralized network inspection

Identity and Access Management.overview: Design and implement comprehensive IAM solutions for authentication and authorization (20% of exam)

key_services.name: AWS IAM
key_services.purpose: Identity and Access Management for secure AWS resource access
key_features: Users, groups, and roles for identity management
Policies (identity-based and resource-based)
Permission boundaries limit maximum permissions
Service control policies (SCPs) in Organizations
IAM Access Analyzer identifies external access
exam_tips: Use roles instead of long-term credentials
Permission boundaries act as guardrails
SCPs affect all principals including root
Access Analyzer detects overly permissive access
Conditions add context-based access control

key_services.name: AWS Organizations
key_features: Organizational units (OUs) for account grouping
Service control policies for governance
Consolidated billing and cost allocation
Delegated administrator accounts
Policy inheritance through OU hierarchy
exam_tips: SCPs don't grant permissions, they limit them
Use separate accounts for workload isolation
Deny statements in SCPs always take precedence
Organization trails simplify multi-account logging

key_services.name: AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO)
key_services.purpose: Centralized single sign-on for multiple AWS accounts
key_features: Built-in identity store or external identity provider
Permission sets for AWS account access
SAML 2.0 support for business applications
Integration with Active Directory
Automatic credential rotation
exam_tips: Eliminates individual IAM users in each account
Permission sets create roles in target accounts
Preferred method for human access to multiple accounts
Supports Azure AD, Okta, OneLogin, and others

key_services.name: Amazon Cognito
key_services.purpose: User identity and authentication for web/mobile apps
key_features: User pools for authentication and user management
Identity pools for AWS credential vending
Social login (Facebook, Google, Amazon, Apple)
SAML and OIDC federation
MFA and advanced security features
exam_tips: User pools authenticate; identity pools authorize
Identity pools provide temporary AWS credentials
Use for consumer-facing applications
Advanced security detects compromised credentials

best_practices: Enable MFA for all human users
Use IAM roles instead of long-term access keys
Implement least privilege access principle
Use permission boundaries for delegated administration
Enable IAM Access Analyzer to identify external access
Rotate credentials regularly
Use AWS SSO for multi-account human access
Implement SCPs in Organizations for governance
Enable CloudTrail to log all IAM API calls
Use resource-based policies for cross-account access

Data Protection.overview: Implement comprehensive data protection including encryption and key management (22% of exam)

key_services.name: AWS KMS
key_services.purpose: Managed service for creating and controlling encryption keys
key_features: Customer managed keys (CMKs) for encryption
Automatic key rotation for CMKs
Key policies and IAM policies for access control
Grants for temporary delegated access
CloudTrail logging of all key usage
FIPS 140-2 Level 2 validated HSMs
exam_tips: CMKs never leave KMS unencrypted
Use envelope encryption for large data
Key policies define who can use/manage keys
Grants provide temporary access without policy changes
Multi-region keys replicate across regions

key_services.name: AWS Secrets Manager
key_services.purpose: Centrally manage secrets with automatic rotation
key_features: Automatic rotation for RDS, Redshift, DocumentDB
Lambda functions for custom rotation logic
Version tracking with automatic rollback
Cross-account access via resource policies
Integration with CloudFormation and ECS
exam_tips: Automatically rotates and updates database passwords
More features than Parameter Store but costs more
Use Lambda for custom secret types
Resource policies enable cross-account access

key_services.name: Amazon Macie
key_services.purpose: Data security service using ML to discover and protect sensitive data
key_features: Automated discovery of PII in S3
ML-based data classification
Custom data identifiers for specific patterns
S3 bucket inventory and security analysis
Findings sent to Security Hub
exam_tips: Scans S3 buckets for sensitive data automatically
Uses managed and custom data identifiers
Helps meet PCI-DSS and GDPR requirements
Can be scheduled for regular scans

key_services.name: AWS Certificate Manager
key_features: Free public certificates for AWS services
Automatic renewal and deployment
Integration with ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway
Private CA for internal certificates
Certificate transparency logging
exam_tips: Public ACM certificates cannot be exported
Private CA allows creating internal certificates
Automatic renewal eliminates manual management
Certificates are regional (except CloudFront)

best_practices: Encrypt data at rest using KMS or CloudHSM
Enforce TLS for data in transit
Use Secrets Manager for credential management
Enable automatic key rotation for KMS keys
Use S3 Block Public Access at account level
Enable versioning and MFA Delete for critical buckets
Use Object Lock for compliance and immutability
Use Macie to discover and protect sensitive data
Implement ACM for certificate lifecycle management
Use CloudTrail to audit all key usage
